parsed.explanation: Section 3 proves only that V contains at most one positive value. It never excludes negative values of g; earlier it records merely g(x)>-x. Thus neither “g≡0” nor “V⊆{0,c}” follows from the established result. The missing fact g(x)≥0 can be proved from (4): if g(x)=d<0, induction gives g(x+nd)=d and hence f^n(x)=x+nd>0 for every n, impossible for sufficiently large n. Since this argument is absent, the later use of b∈{0,c} in Lemma 1 is unjustified, and the necessity proof remains incomplete as written.
